title: The Abduction of Sherlock Holmes: A Dataset for Visual Abductive Reasoning

bias_targets.methodology: Manual close reading of a random sample of 250 dataset inferences to identify assumptions about perceived gender and pronoun usage, as well as filtering 30K samples through the Perspective API to find sexualized or non-traditionally-gendered commentary.
Manual examination of dataset inferences to identify speculation about an individual's race or color based on visual clues (e.g., guessing race based on a sweater logo).
Manual review of sampled annotations to find assumptions about a person's country-of-origin based on visual items (e.g., assuming an individual is from Morocco because they are wearing a fez).
Manual qualitative inspection of annotator inferences to identify age-related assumptions and language (e.g., assuming someone is an 'old man' based on visual context).
Passing 30K samples through the Perspective API for toxicity detection, followed by a manual review of the top 50 most toxic instances, which revealed cases of weight stigmatization.
Passing 30K samples through the Perspective API and manually reviewing the most toxic outputs to identify insensitivity towards mental illness.
